race_context: Sunman-Dearborn Community School Corporation, based in St. Leon, covers about 160 square miles in seven townships (six in Dearborn County and one in Ripley County), including Bright, Dover, Guilford, Hidden Valley Lake, Logan, New Alsace, St. Leon, Sunman, West Harrison and Yorkville. It runs East Central High School, East Central Middle School and Bright, North Dearborn and Sunman elementaries {sd_about}. State enrollment counts were 3,762 students in 2023-24, 3,682 in 2024-25 and 3,659 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}.
Superintendent: Dr. Andrew Jackson; Dr. Kelly Roth became assistant superintendent for curriculum and instruction in a May 2026 reorganization {ec_realign}{sd_min_20260910}.

The board has seven members, each listed by the district as representing a township: James (Jamie) Graf, president (York); Glenn Scholl, vice president (Kelso); Dawn Burke, secretary (Miller); Joseph Bulach (Adams); Robert (Scot) Davis (Harrison); Gary Gellert (Logan); and Sara Hylton (Jackson) {sd_board}{sd_min_20260108}. Ripley County's 2026 sample ballot for an Adams Township precinct lists all three Sunman-Dearborn races (Districts 1, 4 and 5), 'vote for one (1) only,' which indicates that all voters in the corporation vote in every district race; it also notes that a straight-party vote does not count for these offices {ripley_sample}. This guide did not find a published map of which township goes with each district number.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 1 (Joseph Bulach vs. Michael Norman), District 4 (Peter (Pete) Lyness, unopposed) and District 5 (Gary Gellert, unopposed) {in_list}{ic_list}{dc_candlist}. Four members were elected in 2022 for terms ending this year: Bulach, Gellert, Burke and Scholl {enr_2022}. Burke and Scholl are not on the 2026 list {ic_list}, so Lyness is seeking an open seat, and one of the four seats appears to have no candidate on the ballot. This guide could not confirm which of the two (Miller or Kelso township) is District 4.
District 1 is a rematch: in 2022 Bulach unseated Norman, then the board president, 3,482 votes to 2,921 {reg_2022}{enr_2022}.

Party labels: Lyness filed as a Republican; Bulach, Norman and Gellert filed without a party and are listed as Nonpartisan. 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party {ic_list}{in_list}.

Budget and SEA 1 (January 2026): the district's 2026–2030 five-year forecast said recent state property-tax reform 'has already begun to reduce the district's projected funding,' but projected positive balances in the Education, Operations and Rainy Day funds through 2030 and no cuts to student programs, relying on 'aligning staffing with enrollment trends and managing compensation growth' {ec_forecast}. Jackson said the board's planning left the district 'in a strong position to weather this storm' {ec_forecast}. The board adopted the 2026 budget in October 2025 and held the 2027 budget hearing on Sept. 10, 2026; no member of the public commented {sd_min_20251002}{sd_min_20260910}.

Teacher pay (November 2025): the board approved a two-year contract with the Sunman-Dearborn Educators Association setting starting pay at $49,500 for 2025-26 and $50,000 for 2026-27, which the district called the highest in the region, with raises of $1,500 to $3,000 for returning teachers {ec_cba}{sd_min_20251113}.

Facilities: the district completed phase one of a building project in 2023 and began a second phase of about $33 million, mostly mechanical replacements, which it said would be financed without raising the tax rate {ec_phase1}{ec_phase2}. In 2025 that work included a new library at East Central High School, a turf soccer field and a new Bright Elementary playground {ec_upgrades}. The board held hearings on another project in February 2026 and adopted a final bond resolution on Sept. 10, 2026; the minutes do not describe the project or its cost {sd_min_20260212}{sd_min_20260219}{sd_min_20260910}.

Policies (2025–2026): in October 2025 the board voted 5-2 (Burke and Gellert opposed) to allow a board member's relative to be employed as superintendent if that member stays out of the discussion and vote and both file conflict-of-interest statements {sd_min_20251002}. In September 2026 it began adopting a policy that school facilities will not be named after individuals, after a public request in August to name the football field after a former coach's father {sd_min_20260813}{sd_min_20260910}. The board also joined litigation against social media companies and approved a district daycare and learning center {sd_min_20260910}{sd_min_20260312}.

Academics: the superintendent's message on the district website says Sunman-Dearborn received an 'A' on the most recent state report card {sd_home}. At the Aug. 13, 2026 meeting Jackson congratulated all three elementary schools on their IREAD results {sd_min_20260813}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or voter-guide entries for these races. The Dearborn County Register's candidate listings are behind a paywall.

background: Won the seat in 2022 by defeating then-board president Michael Norman {reg_2022}{enr_2022}.

path_to_ballot: Filed June 9, 2026 without declaring a party; the state lists him as Nonpartisan {ic_list}{in_list}.

items: Moved the 2026 board pay ($150 per regular meeting, $75 per special meeting or work session, and a $2,000 annual stipend), which passed on a voice vote {sd_min_20260108}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, unopposed; elected in 2018 and 2022 and listed by the district as representing Logan Township {enr_2018}{enr_2022}{sd_board}.
background: Served on the team for the district's 2022–2027 strategic plan {sd_home}.
path_to_ballot: Filed June 11, 2026 without declaring a party; the state lists him as Nonpartisan {ic_list}{in_list}.

items: In March 2026 he said the Science of Reading 'is a good thing,' but that a state ban on cell phones all day 'is an overreach by the Indiana General Assembly' and the board needs 'to speak up for local control' (as summarized in the board minutes) {sd_min_20260312}.
At the September 2025 budget hearing he asked how the 2026 budget compared with the year before; Jackson said it was slightly lower because the district paid off its pension debt {sd_min_20250916}.
In June 2026 he said he was glad the district is hiring teachers who graduated from East Central {sd_min_20260611}.
In October 2025 he and Burke voted against the policy option allowing a board member's relative to be employed as superintendent; it passed 5-2 {sd_min_20251002}.
